title: IC Substrate Inspection - Delamination Detection on Teron SL650
subtitle: Post-Etch Quality Validation for 14nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Thomas Mueller

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Teron SL650 system to detect and classify Delamination defects during post-etch inspection at the 14nm technology node. The test is conducted at Dresden Fab 3 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 300mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Delamination defects that are critical to yield at the 14nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Teron SL650 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Teron SL650
- Inspection Type: IC Substrate Inspection
- Target Defect: Delamination
- Process Step: Post-Etch
- Wafer Size: 300mm
- Technology Node: 14nm
- Fab Location: Dresden Fab 3

This test case applies to all Teron SL650 systems deployed at Dresden Fab 3 for post-etch monitoring in the 14nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Teron SL650
Software Version: v15.2.273
Recipe: IC_SUBSTRATE_INSPECTION_14nm_POST_ETCH
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: Medium (150 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 1.0μm
Edge Exclusion: 2mm
Sampling Plan: 21-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Teron SL650 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'IC Substrate Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Delamination defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 14nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 60 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 96% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±2.0% for IC Substrate Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.99 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-03-01
Wafers Tested: 14
Total Defects Found: 873
Defect Density: 123.5 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 4.5%
Capture Rate: 97.7%
Test Duration: 395 minutes
System Uptime: 97.6%

Result Classification: CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Teron SL650 demonstrated acceptable performance in detecting Delamination at the 14nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) Edge-zone defect detection showed improved performance compared to previous revision.

e) The defect review station correlation was within specification.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
